method: Use unseasoned mince made from 100% skinless turkey breast, weighed raw. Commercial mixed-cut turkey mince is not the specified ingredient; ask the butcher for breast mince or mince skinless breast at home.
Wash and dry the lettuce and tomato. Shred the lettuce and slice the tomato; put both on a clean plate, separate from the raw filling.
Split the wholemeal burger bun and toast the cut faces in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 1–2 minutes. Set it on a clean plate.

Press the turkey breast mince into a patty about 1.5cm thick, slightly wider than the bun; no binder is needed. Coat with all the measured paprika, chilli powder, garlic powder and dried oregano. After handling raw turkey breast mince, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Heat the measured olive oil in the non-stick frying pan. Cook the turkey patty over a medium heat for about 5–6 minutes on each side, turning carefully. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must stay at 75°C or above for 30 seconds. Without a thermometer, cut the thickest piece open and check that it is steaming inside with no pink meat. Continue cooking until these checks are met; the suggested pan time alone is not a safety check.
Put the lettuce and tomato in the toasted bun, add the cooked turkey patty, then close the bun and serve immediately.

review.notes: One browned cooked turkey-mince patty with dried-spice coating, shredded lettuce and sliced tomato in plain unseeded wholemeal bun; no sauce or cheese. Believable single serving with central composition and crop margin.
review.alt: Spiced turkey burger with lettuce and tomato in a wholemeal bun.
